requirement: A `{req}` definition MUST use an opening fence of at least three colons immediately followed by `{req} <name>`. A closing fence MUST have at least as many colons as the opening fence and nothing else on its line except whitespace. As in CommonMark fences, an opening or closing fence MAY be indented by up to three spaces; a line indented by four or more spaces MUST NOT be a fence. The requirement body MUST be all Markdown between those fence lines, including headings, examples, diagrams, and blank lines, and MUST NOT include text after the closing fence. Leading and trailing whitespace MUST be excluded when comparing the body with evidence.
rationale:
## Obligation assessment

- **Opening fence: at least three colons, immediately followed by `{req} <name>`.** `src/lib.rs#fn[definition_blocks]` and its helper `src/lib.rs#fn[colon_fence]`, reachable from `src/evidence.rs#fn[collect_definitions]`, enforce these properties. `src/lib.rs#mod[tests]/fn[closing_fences_allow_no_trailing_text_and_fences_allow_three_spaces_of_indent]` tests valid syntax, two colons, intervening whitespace, and missing whitespace before the name.
- **Closing fence: at least the opener's colon count; only whitespace otherwise.** `src/lib.rs#fn[definition_blocks]` checks both properties. The preceding test covers trailing text and whitespace; `src/lib.rs#mod[tests]/fn[a_longer_colon_fence_contains_a_shorter_nested_directive]` covers a shorter colon line remaining in the body. However, the test exercising a strictly longer closer, `src/evidence.rs#mod[tests]/fn[validates_four_or_more_colon_fences_and_longer_closers]`, references only `requirements.ci.fence_lengths`. It needs a `{test}` reference to `requirements.ci.span` to cover this subject's expressly specified boundary case.
- **Four-or-more-space indentation must not constitute either fence.** `src/lib.rs#fn[colon_fence]` rejects it. `src/lib.rs#mod[tests]/fn[closing_fences_allow_no_trailing_text_and_fences_allow_three_spaces_of_indent]` asserts rejection for both opening and closing fences and acceptance at three spaces.
- **The body must contain all intervening Markdown, including headings, examples, diagrams, and blank lines.** `src/lib.rs#fn[definition_blocks]` computes the intervening byte range, preserving Markdown without distinctions among those content types. The Markdown-preservation tests are `src/evidence.rs#mod[tests]/fn[validates_full_names_requirement_text_and_input_lines]` and `src/evidence.rs#mod[tests]/fn[colon_requirement_span_includes_markdown_and_excludes_following_text]`. Nevertheless, `src/evidence.rs#fn[collect_definitions]` passes that range through `src/lib.rs#fn[without_options]`, which deletes option-shaped lines identified by `src/lib.rs#fn[option_line]`. Thus intervening Markdown such as an initial `:note: explanatory text` is removed rather than retained. The subject provides no exception to its all-Markdown obligation for such lines. This is a substantive gap.
- **Text after the closing fence must not enter the body.** The range ends at the closing line's start in `src/lib.rs#fn[definition_blocks]`; the span test above and the shorter-nested-directive test assert exclusion of following text.
- **Leading and trailing whitespace must be excluded for body comparison.** `src/evidence.rs#fn[collect_definitions]` applies `.trim()` to the extracted text. `src/evidence.rs#mod[tests]/fn[requirement_bodies_are_compared_without_surrounding_whitespace]` verifies that surrounding body whitespace does not affect matching evidence.

The missing-closing-fence case is additionally tested by `src/evidence.rs#mod[tests]/fn[reports_a_missing_closing_colon_fence]`.

Neither the body-deletion gap nor the missing subject reference on the longer-closer test is acknowledged by a supplied `{fixme}`.

text: A `{req}` definition MUST use an opening fence of at least three colons immediately followed by `{req} <name>`. A closing fence MUST have at least as many colons as the opening fence and nothing else on its line except whitespace. As in CommonMark fences, an opening or closing fence MAY be indented by up to three spaces; a line indented by four or more spaces MUST NOT be a fence. The requirement body MUST be all Markdown between those fence lines, including headings, examples, diagrams, and blank lines, and MUST NOT include text after the closing fence. Leading and trailing whitespace MUST be excluded when comparing the body with evidence.
The `requirement` string in each evidence file MUST match all Markdown inside its fenced `{req}` directive, excluding leading and trailing whitespace. Habeas MUST report changed requirement text.

A `{req}` opening fence MAY contain four or more colons. Habeas MUST accept opening fences of any length of at least three colons. A colon-only line with fewer colons than the opener MUST remain inside the requirement body, allowing a nested colon directive. A closing fence outside a fenced code example with at least as many colons as the opener MUST end the body.

An mdBook chapter MAY declare a named definition using a fenced `{definition}` directive. Definitions MUST use the same chapter-qualified names, identifier rules, fence rules, and nonempty-body rules as requirements and examples. Names MUST be unique across all three kinds.

Each definition MUST declare exactly one nonempty `:phrase:` option before its explanatory body. The phrase MUST be interpreted as plain text. Definitions MUST NOT require their own evidence records or determinations.

For a requirements input, `requirements` MUST be a {term}`requirements.references.definition_selection`, and Habeas MUST match it against all defined requirements and named examples. It MUST recompute the matches during validation, sort their full names, and compare them with `matches`. It MUST take each match's complete raw fenced declaration, including its opening and closing lines, concatenate those declarations in full-name order with one blank line between them, and compare the resulting raw lines with `text`. It MUST retain every match's current source file and inclusive line range for display and reference coverage. A selection matching no definitions MUST be invalid. Adding, removing, renaming, or changing a matched definition MUST invalidate the stored input; moving an unchanged declaration within the book MUST NOT. Errors MUST identify the selection and affected definitions when available.
